transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I haven’t really been myself. I keep getting irritated and snapping at people over small things—like on operations calls, and even at home with my family. I don’t mean to make it sound worse than it is, but… it’s not how I usually handle things, and it’s starting to worry me.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things that usually bring you pleasure?

I wouldn’t say I’m, you know, completely depressed or anything… but yeah, I guess things don’t really land the same. Like my wife will make dinner, or my kids are talking about soccer like they always do, and I know I should feel happy to be there with them. I want to. But it’s like there’s nothing in me that responds. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed that you feel tired or have less energy than usual, even after getting enough rest?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m not trying to rest. I do get in bed, but most nights I just lie there and it’s like I can still hear that alarm in my head. Then if I finally drift off, I wake up sweating from dreams—smoke, people yelling… things like that.

So by morning, I guess, yeah… I feel like I barely slept at all. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any trouble focusing or thinking clearly lately, like it’s harder to make decisions or follow through on tasks?

Yeah… a little. I mean, I’m still trying to keep up and not make excuses, but I haven’t been cleared to go back to the plant yet, and even working from home I’m missing things on calls that I normally wouldn’t.

I’ll lose track of what someone just said, or I’ll forget to follow up on something, and then people get frustrated. I know that’s not fair to them. I just… I’m worried I’m starting to be more of a liability than the manager they need right now. Does that make sense?
Have you experienced or witnessed any particularly stressful or traumatic event recently—something like a serious accident, a fire, or anything that left you feeling shaken or unsafe?

Yeah… there was an incident at the facility. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but there was a valve failure and someone got hurt.

That was about three weeks ago, and I guess things have been… off since then. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of event you’re asking about.
Since the incident at the facility, have you been avoiding reminders of it—like certain places, conversations, or thoughts—or have you felt emotionally numb or detached from others more often?

I don’t know if I’d call it avoiding exactly… I mean, I’m trying to act normal around everyone.

But, yeah, there’s this numbness, I guess. My wife will make dinner, or my kids will start talking about soccer like they always do, and I know I should feel happy to be there with them. I want to. But it’s like… nothing in me really responds.

I’m not trying to be cold. It just feels like I’m not fully there. Is that… is that what you mean?
Since the incident, have you noticed that you’re more irritable or angry than usual, or that you blame yourself for things more often?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m out of control or anything, but… yes.

That’s actually part of why I’m here. I keep blowing up at people over things that shouldn’t set me off. I’ll snap on operations calls, and then afterward I’m sitting there thinking, what is wrong with me? And it’s happened at home too, with my wife and the kids, over nothing really.

That’s not how I’ve ever handled things. I’m not proud of it. I just… I don’t want to be that guy.
Since the incident at the facility, have you found yourself being more on edge or easily startled by things that wouldn’t have bothered you before?

Yeah… I guess I have. I don’t want to sound dramatic, but little sounds set me off now.

Like if I hear a forklift backing up, or a compressor kick on, my whole body just tightens before I even think about it. Even at home, the smoke alarm did that little chirp the other night and I was immediately looking around like, okay, where’s the exit, what’s going wrong?

I know that probably sounds… excessive. But that’s what happens.
Have you found yourself losing interest in activities or things you used to enjoy, even things that were important to you?

Yeah… I mean, maybe not interest exactly. I still try to do the normal things, be with my family, sit down for dinner, listen when the kids talk about soccer.

But it’s like I’m not getting anything back from it inside. My wife will make dinner, or the kids are talking like they always do, and I know I should feel glad to be there. I want to. I’m trying to.

It’s just… there’s nothing in me that really responds. I don’t know if that answers what you’re asking.
Have you found yourself not wanting to do things you used to enjoy, or feeling like those activities don’t bring you any real pleasure anymore?

Yeah… I think that’s fair.

I still do the things, or I try to. Like my wife will make dinner, or the kids are talking about soccer like they always do, and I know I should feel happy to be there with them. I want to feel that.

But it’s like… nothing in me really responds. Not the way it used to. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
